correctness.rationale: Odd-frequency antisymmetry converts nonnegativity of 1+Q into |Q|<=1. Evaluations at 0 and pi/4 give the sharp upper bound. Equality forces both contacts and a derivative condition, uniquely fixing all coefficients. An exact Q(sqrt(2)) factorization proves the candidate satisfies |Q|<=1 on the entire interval; no finite sampling is used to prove the universal statement.

value.rationale: The quantity is a natural exact invariant for the first nontrivial finite support consisting of the two lowest additional odd harmonics. The 2003 source explicitly treats prescribed finite higher-frequency sets as the underlying extremal objects and poses fixed-cardinality extremal questions. The exact value supplies a concrete sharp benchmark between the known singleton and full-odd regimes, and the two-contact certificate plus uniqueness identifies the complete extremal geometry rather than merely recomputing a table entry.
